title: [Chapitre] IV. Analysis situs (première mouture) : notes manuscrites (10/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: in this 1986 first draft of 'Analysis situs', Grothendieck is building an axiomatic theory of 'figures' (finite stratified objects) inside an ambient set M of 'multiplicités' (multi-strata). The objects and relations are as follows.
- F̄ denotes the set of (multi)strata of a figure F.
- X ≤ F means X is a stratum of F, or later that F is refined or subdivided.
- ≪ is an 'induced subfigure / factorisation' relation, with F_Y the subfigure of F induced by (the inverse image of) Y.
- ≼ is a third relation introduced by axioms C5–C7.

(1) Corollary closing the argument of p.79. Let F ≪ G. For each stratum X ∈ F̄, the previous page showed the following: among the strata Y of G with X ≪ Y there is a minimal one (existence by finiteness of combinatorial dimension), and it is unique. Uniqueness follows from the 'familiar property' F_Y ∩ F_{Y'} = F_{Y∩Y'}, so two candidates Y, Y' both lead to Y∩Y', and minimality forces equality. Hence a well-defined map φ: F̄ → Ḡ, X ↦ the smallest stratum Y of G with X ≪ Y. It is monotone ('croissante', 'trivial'): X ≤ X' ≪ φ(X') gives X ≪ φ(X'), so φ(X) ≤ φ(X'). In modern terms this is the 'carrier' or support map from the face poset of a figure to the face poset of a figure it maps into: each cell goes to the smallest closed cell containing its image. It is the standard carrier map of a cellular or stratified map.

(2) Meta-remark. So far axioms C5, C6, C7 (introducing ≼, ≪) are satisfied by trivial interpretations, e.g. ≼ = inclusion of figures, or equality. It is 'time to come to more specific properties'.

(3) 14 June. First, a notational change: F̃ replaces F̄ for {X ∈ M : X ≤ F}, to avoid confusion with topological closure ('adhérence'). Second, a corollary of 'prop. 4' / axiom C4 (p.47). For a chain of refinements G' ≤ G ≤ F, any (multi)stratum common to G' and F is a stratum of G, i.e. G̃' ∩ F̃ ⊂ G̃. This is a convexity property of the refinement order with respect to strata: a stratum of the finest and of the coarsest figure survives in every intermediate one. A proof is sketched: X is a stratum of a refinement of F, hence of a refinement G_1 of G induced by a refinement (axiom C6). The proof is broken off at 'Supposons X ≤ F' and resumed on p.81 via inverse images G_X ≤ X and a minimality axiom C8: a multiplicity admits no proper subdivision, i.e. X ≤ Φ forces X = Φ.

Check against PL topology: for subdivisions of polyhedral complexes K'' ◁ K' ◁ K, a cell σ of both K'' and K is a cell of K'. The open cell of σ lies in a unique open cell τ of K'. τ is a union of cells of K'' and is contained in an open cell of K, which must be σ, so τ = σ. The statement is therefore correct and standard.
errors: The displayed formula 'Ḡ' ∩ F̄ = Ḡ' cannot be literally right: Ḡ is not in general contained in Ḡ'. The intended statement is Ḡ' ∩ F̄ ⊂ Ḡ, i.e. common strata of the finest and coarsest figure are strata of the intermediate one.

The parenthetical 'donc G̃' ∩ F̃ = G̃' ∩ G̃' as written would also require every common stratum of G' and G to be a stratum of F, which is false in general. The correct consequence is G̃' ∩ F̃ = G̃' ∩ G̃ ∩ F̃ (or simply ⊂ G̃).
The proof of the 14 June corollary is not completed on this page. Several attempts are struck out and it is resumed on p.81.

ideas.what: Map φ sending a stratum X of F to the smallest stratum of G through which X factors (X ≪ Y), shown to be well defined and monotone
ideas.modern_name: carrier / support map between face posets (cellular carrier) of a stratified or cellular map
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical combinatorial topology (carrier notion: Alexandroff–Hopf, Lefschetz); standard for stratified maps
ideas.where_published: Unpublished; the Esquisse d'un programme only announces a programme of tame topology.

ideas.what: Convexity of strata along a refinement chain: G' ≤ G ≤ F implies strata common to G' and F are strata of G
ideas.modern_name: convexity property of subdivisions/refinements of stratifications (standard in PL topology)

ideas.what: Axiomatic framework of 'figures', 'multiplicités', relations ≤, ≼, ≪ with axioms C4–C8 as a foundation for tame topology
ideas.modern_name: axiomatic tame topology / combinatorial stratified spaces (cf. o-minimal structures, exit-path posets)
ideas.usually_credited_to: o-minimality: van den Dries, Pillay–Steinhorn, Knight (1980s); tame topology programme announced by Grothendieck in the Esquisse
ideas.where_published: Programme announced in Esquisse d'un programme (1984), §5–6; this specific axiomatics unpublished

missed.claim: Grothendieck notes that his axioms C5–C7 are still satisfied by degenerate interpretations (≼ = inclusion, or equality) and that 'more specific' axioms are needed. The axiom system for figures/multiplicités was never completed or published. It remains a possible alternative, purely order-theoretic foundation for tame topology, distinct from o-minimality.
missed.quote: il serait temps d'en venir à des propriétés plus spécifiques !
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Combinatorial or axiomatic models of stratified spaces (exit-path categories, conically stratified spaces, o-minimal triangulations) are active topics. The draft's axiomatics could be compared with these, but the individual results on this page are standard.

deep.surprise_reason: The page contains routine lemmas (carrier map; convexity of strata under refinement) inside an unpublished axiomatic tame-topology draft. Interesting historically as evidence of the axiomatic approach, but nothing new to a specialist on this page.
